"""Identifier case conversion."""

from __future__ import annotations


def snake_case(text: str) -> str:
    """Convert an identifier or phrase to ``snake_case``.

    Spaces, hyphens and underscores separate words. A change from a
    lowercase letter or a digit to an uppercase letter also separates
    words (``helloWorld`` -> ``hello_world``). A run of consecutive
    uppercase letters belongs to a single word; the run is split only
    when it is immediately followed by a capitalised word, e.g.
    ``XMLHttpRequest`` -> ``xml_http_request`` and ``HTTPServer`` ->
    ``http_server``. The result is lowercase, never contains two
    underscores in a row, and never starts or ends with one.

    Args:
        text: Input identifier, e.g. ``camelCase``, ``PascalCase`` or
            ``kebab-case``.

    Returns:
        The ``snake_case`` form of ``text``.
    """
    words: list[str] = []
    word: list[str] = []
    n = len(text)

    def flush() -> None:
        if word:
            words.append("".join(word))
            del word[:]

    for index, char in enumerate(text):
        if not char.isalnum():
            flush()
            continue
        if char.isupper():
            prev = text[index - 1] if index else ""
            next_char = text[index + 1] if index + 1 < n else ""
            # A lowercase letter or digit before the uppercase letter.
            new_word = index > 0 and (prev.islower() or prev.isdigit())
            # The last letter of an acronym run directly before a
            # capitalised word (e.g. the ``P`` in ``HTTPServer``).
            if not new_word:
                new_word = (
                    index > 0
                    and prev.isupper()
                    and index + 1 < n
                    and next_char.islower()
                )
            if new_word:
                flush()
        word.append(char.lower())
    flush()
    return "_".join(words).strip("_")
